takeaway: Windy, sunny and hot. A cold-air push over the Caribbean has the trade winds cranking: Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) put out a wind warning, with gusts of 40–70 km/h near the mountains, and Nicoya near 35°C. The beach stays dry through at least Wednesday. For surf, the trades stay offshore at Nosara, strongest tonight through Saturday morning, then easing from Saturday night, a day earlier than yesterday's call. Friday's new southwest swell plus strong offshore looks like the pick. New today: most models show a weak low just off northwest Costa Rica around Dec 1–2 and a few light showers creeping toward the Nicoya coast around Dec 3–7. Worth watching, but no rainy spell is expected.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Thu Nov 26 – Sat Nov 28)
periods.pattern: Cold surge #5 is moving through northern Central America and the Caribbean and boosting the trades. IMN calls the North Pacific clear and sunny today with occasional gusts all day, and strong gusts of 40–70 km/h near the mountain ranges. The marine forecast has northeast to east winds of 20–25 knots in the Papagayo area today through Saturday, pulsing near gale force tonight through Saturday morning, with a chance of gale force tonight and Friday night. The extra wind pushes rain onto the Caribbean side: IMN expects scattered rain on the Caribbean coast and in the Northern Zone from this afternoon, and the European and AI ensemble averages show about 30–40 mm near Limón in the 24 hours ending Friday evening. Every model keeps Nicoya at a trace.
periods.implications: Sunny and hot: about 35°C at Nicoya, low 30s at the beach, about 22°C at night. Windy and dusty, with the strongest gusts tonight through Saturday morning. Good for outdoor plans if you can handle wind. Bring sun protection and water, not rain gear. Rough water for boats and paddling.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Sun Nov 29 – Wed Dec 2)
periods.pattern: The trades ease. The marine forecast drops Papagayo winds to 15–20 knots Saturday night and Sunday, 10–15 knots Sunday night, a brief bump to 15–20 knots Monday, then 10–15 knots Monday night. IMN's weekly outlook (Nov 26–30) still calls the North Pacific stable and dry, highs up to about 36°C. Most models, all but the AI ensemble, now show a weak low just off the Papagayo and Nicoya coast around Dec 1–2. It sits inside the east wind stream, and the wind over Costa Rica stays easterly. Rain at Nicoya stays at a trace to light in every model.
periods.implications: Breezy Sunday, calmer Monday night through Wednesday. Boat and paddle trips get easier from Sunday afternoon. Still very dry: tie down loose gear and be careful with fire. Rain at the beach is unlikely.
periods.confidence: High on dry. Moderate on how fast the wind eases.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Thu Dec 3 – Thu Dec 10)
periods.pattern: Mostly dry season, with a small wrinkle around Dec 3–7. The ensemble averages bring a band of rain from the open Pacific closer to southern Costa Rica and show light rain near the Nicoya coast: about 5–10 mm a day in the US ensemble average around Dec 4–6, and about 5–8 mm on Dec 4 in the European and AI averages. Averages spread a few wetter runs over the whole area, so this likely means a few spotty showers at most, mostly offshore. The main European model keeps Nosara at a trace to light. The US ensemble shows a weak low about 450 km west-southwest of Nicoya around Dec 6, and the east wind over Costa Rica holds in every ensemble through Dec 10. IMN's monthly outlook (Nov 30–Dec 27) is unchanged: dry, 0–50 mm a week on the North Pacific, a low chance of extreme rain, 3–3.5°C above normal, moderate wind the first week of December and very light wind with very dry air after that.
periods.implications: Plan freely. Hot and sunny most days. Around Dec 3–7, a passing shower or more clouds is possible, but don't count on rain for the garden. Calmer winds make Dec 3 onward good for boat trips.
periods.confidence: High on mostly dry. Low on whether any showers reach Nosara Dec 3–7.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trade winds (northeast to east), offshore at Nosara, for the whole period. Strongest today through Saturday morning, easing from Saturday night, lighter Dec 2–6, then a steady east wind again toward Dec 10. No lasting Pacific onshore pattern, but a lighter, more variable stretch around Dec 3–6 could bring earlier sea breezes and some choppy afternoons.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued about 3:45 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast to east winds of 20–25 knots today through Saturday, near gale force tonight through Saturday morning. Then 15–20 knots Saturday night and Sunday, 10–15 knots Sunday night, 15–20 knots Monday. Off Nicoya and to the south, winds are light and variable (under 5 knots) this morning, turning west around 10 knots late tonight and west to northwest around 10 knots Friday. So the offshore reaches Nosara over the land, not along the coast, and Friday's afternoon breeze may turn it side-on sooner. Swell (open-ocean numbers, not beach heights): southwest 5–7 ft at 17 seconds tonight, 6–8 ft at 17 seconds Friday, 6–8 ft at 13 seconds Saturday, then 4–6 ft at 15 seconds Sunday and 3–5 ft Monday. The big wave numbers in the Papagayo forecast are wind chop blowing out of the gulf, not surf for Nosara. Nicaragua is likely offshore all day today through Saturday. That points to clean, strong Nosara mornings, not all-day offshore here. Tides are easing toward the last-quarter moon.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today to Saturday Nov 28: dawn to late morning, possibly past noon, but strong and gusty. Friday's new swell plus strong offshore is the pick; go early. Sunday Nov 29 and Monday Nov 30: dawn to mid-morning. Dec 1–6: early mornings only, with lighter trades and earlier sea breeze. Dec 7–10: dawn to mid-morning as the east wind firms up again.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore mornings through Monday. Moderate on afternoon breeze timing. Low to moderate on wind direction Dec 3–6.

gyreWatch.status: Not expected. Watch only, low chance. No prolonged rainy spell expected.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: If anything, Dec 1–7. The US hurricane center expects no storm formation near Central America in the next 7 days (its only system is far away in the central Pacific, 10% chance). The global tropics outlook (Nov 24, unchanged) flags a 20–40% chance of a storm in early December, but far west in the open Pacific, more than 1,500 miles from Costa Rica.
gyreWatch.supporting: Most models show a weak low just off northwest Costa Rica around Dec 1–2. The US ensemble shows another weak low about 450 km west-southwest of Nicoya around Dec 6. The ensemble averages edge light rain toward the Nicoya coast Dec 3–7. The tropics outlook says upper-level conditions over the Americas may turn a bit more favorable for storms in weeks 2–3.
gyreWatch.conflicting: The east wind over Costa Rica holds in every ensemble through Dec 10, so the lows stay offshore and don't pull in wet southwest flow. The AI ensemble shows no low near Costa Rica. The main European model keeps Nosara at a trace to light. IMN expects no extreme events Nov 30–Dec 6, dry weeks ahead, and a strong El Niño keeps favoring a dry December.

whatChanged: The strong-trade stretch got shorter but sharper: near gale force tonight through Saturday morning, then easing from Saturday night instead of holding through Sunday. IMN issued a wind warning last evening for the cold surge. New today: most models show a weak low just off northwest Costa Rica around Dec 1–2, and the ensemble averages now show light showers near the Nicoya coast around Dec 3–7, up from a trace yesterday. So the rain watch moves from "no watch needed" to "watch only, low chance". IMN's weekly and monthly outlooks and the global tropics outlook are unchanged. Still no storms near Costa Rica.
practical: Surf early, especially Friday. Expect wind and dust through Saturday, with rough water for boats. Sunday afternoon onward gets calmer. Plan outdoor events freely; around Dec 3–7, have a backup for a passing shower, but expect mostly dry. Stay hydrated and avoid open burning.
